stimuli.text:
A `PunchCard` represents a prepaid card for a number of visits. Each successful `punch` uses one visit. After every 3 successful punches, the card earns one free visit.


• `PunchCard(int visits)` creates a card with the given number of visits.

• `boolean punch()` uses a visit and returns true if one is available; otherwise it changes nothing and returns false.

• `int getRemaining()` returns the number of visits left.

For example, after `PunchCard c = new PunchCard(4);`, calling `c.punch()` 6 times returns true, true, true, true, true, false, and then `c.getRemaining()` returns 0.

questions.stem: A survey app stores users' names together with their answers to sensitive questions. Which practice best reduces harm if the stored data is stolen?

options.text: Keep the data forever in case it is needed
options.why: Keeping data longer increases risk.

options.text: Store answers without names, or encrypt the data
options.why: Correct. Removing identifiers or encrypting limits the damage of a breach.

options.text: Print the data so there is a paper copy
options.why: A paper copy adds another place for the data to leak.

options.text: Ask more sensitive questions so the data is more useful
options.why: This increases the potential harm.

questions.explanation: Removing identifiers or encrypting limits the damage of a breach.
